arxiv-2101-06757.title: Higher Order Automatic Differentiation of Higher Order Functions Thanks: The authors contributed equally to this work.
arxiv-2101-06757.creator: Mathieu Huot, Sam Staton, Matthijs Vákár
arxiv-2101-06757.description: Abstract . We present semantic correctness proofs of automatic differentiation (AD). We consider a forward-mode AD method on a higher order language with algebraic data types, and we characterise it as the unique structure preserving macro given a choice of derivatives for basic operations. We describe a rich semantics for differentiable programming, based on diffeological spaces.

arxiv-2112-03404.title: Learning to Detect Critical Nodes in Sparse Graphs via Feature Importance Awareness
arxiv-2112-03404.creator: Xuwei Tan, Yangming Zhou, MengChu Zhou, Zhang-Hua Fu
arxiv-2112-03404.description: Abstract Detecting critical nodes in sparse graphs is important in a variety of application domains, such as network vulnerability assessment, epidemic control, and drug design. The critical node problem (CNP) aims to find a set of critical nodes from a network whose deletion maximally degrades the pairwise connectivity of the residual network.

arxiv-2203-10197.title: Cost Function Learning in Memorized Social Networks with Cognitive Behavioral Asymmetry
arxiv-2203-10197.creator: Yanbing Mao, Jinning Li, Naira Hovakimyan, Tarek Abdelzaher, Christian Lebiere
arxiv-2203-10197.description: Abstract This paper investigates the cost function learning in social information networks, wherein the human memory and cognitive bias are explicitly taken into account. We first propose a model for social information-diffusion dynamics, with a focus on systematic modeling of asymmetric cognitive bias represented by confirmation bias and novelty bias.

arxiv-2304-07933.title: A structural study of hcp and liquid iron under shock compression up to 275 GPa Journal: Physical Review B
arxiv-2304-07933.creator: Saransh Singh, Richard Briggs, Martin G. Gorman, Lorin X. Benedict, Christine J. Wu, Sebastien Hamel, Amy L. Coleman, Federica Coppari, Amalia Fernandez-Pañella, Christopher McGuire, Melissa Sims, June K. Wicks, Jon H. Eggert, Dayne E. Fratanduono, Raymond F. Smith
arxiv-2304-07933.description: Abstract We combine nanosecond laser shock compression with in-situ picosecond X-ray diffraction to provide structural data on iron up to 275 GPa. We constrain the extent of hcp-liquid coexistence, the onset of total melt, and the structure within the liquid phase. Our results indicate that iron, under shock compression, melts completely by 258(8) GPa.

arxiv-2402-17649.title: Beyond Prompt Brittleness: Evaluating the Reliability and Consistency of Political Worldviews in LLMs
arxiv-2402-17649.creator: Tanise Ceron, Neele Falk, Ana Barić, Dmitry Nikolaev, Sebastian Padó
arxiv-2402-17649.description: Abstract Due to the widespread use of large language models (LLMs), we need to understand whether they embed a specific “worldview” and what these views reflect. Recent studies report that, prompted with political questionnaires, LLMs show left-liberal leanings Feng et al. 2023 ; Motoki et al. 2024 .

arxiv-2501-05125.title: Detection of thioacetaldehyde (CH 3 CHS) in TMC-1 : sulfur-oxygen differentiation along the hydrogenation sequence Thanks: Based on observations carried out with the Yebes 40m telescope (projects 19A003, 20A014, 20D023, 21A011, 21D005, and 23A024). The 40m radio telescope at Yebes Observatory is ope
arxiv-2501-05125.creator: M. Agúndez, G. Molpeceres, C. Cabezas, N. Marcelino, B. Tercero, R. Fuentetaja, P. de Vicente, J. Cernicharo
arxiv-2501-05125.description: Abstract In recent years the chemistry of sulfur in the interstellar medium has experienced a renewed interest due to the detection of a large variety of molecules containing sulfur. Here we report the first identification in space of a new S-bearing molecule, thioacetaldehyde (CH 3 CHS), which is the sulfur counterpart of acetaldehyde (CH 3 CHO).

arxiv-2504-16748.title: Simple Graph Contrastive Learning via Fractional-order Neural Diffusion Networks
arxiv-2504-16748.creator: Yanan Zhao, Ji Feng, Kai Zhao, Xuhao Li, Qiyu Kang, Wenfei Liang, Yahya Alkhatib, Xingchao Jian, Wee Peng Tay
arxiv-2504-16748.description: Abstract Graph Contrastive Learning (GCL) has recently made progress as an unsupervised graph representation learning paradigm. GCL approaches can be categorized into augmentation-based and augmentation-free methods. The former relies on complex data augmentations, while the latter depends on encoders that can generate distinct views of the same input. Both approaches may require negative samples for training.

arxiv-2507-18284.title: Designing Value-Aligned Traffic Agents through Conflict Sensitivity
arxiv-2507-18284.creator: Astrid Rakow, Joe Collenette, Maike Schwammberger, Marija Slavkovik, Gleifer Vaz Alves
arxiv-2507-18284.description: Abstract Autonomous traffic agents ( A​T​As ) are expected to act in ways that are not only safe, but also aligned with stakeholder values across legal, social, and moral dimensions. In this paper, we adopt an established formal model of conflict from epistemic game theory to support the development of such agents.

arxiv-2509-14549.title: Extrapolating Exclusive Charmonium Photoproduction to the Forward Regime Using Gaussian Process
arxiv-2509-14549.creator: Xue Wang, Xu Cao, Yu Lu, Weizhi Xiong
arxiv-2509-14549.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xue Wang, Xu Cao, Yu Lu, Weizhi Xiong. Accessing the forward kinematic regime of exclusive vector meson photoproduction is essential for probing the structure of the proton, yet this region is often experimentally inaccessible. We present a novel extrapolation of near-threshold γ ​ p → J / ψ ​ p \gamma p\to J/\psi p differential cross section data to the forward regime d ​ σ / d ​ t | t = 0 d\sigma/dt|_{t=0} by applying a non-parametric Gaussian Process (GP) regression.

arxiv-2512-04298.title: Experimental Sensitivity Enhancement of a Quantum Rydberg Atom-Based RF Receiver with a Metamaterial GRIN Lens
arxiv-2512-04298.creator: Anton Tishchenko, Demos Serghiou, Ashwin Thelappilly Joy, Paul Marsh, Paul Martin, Tim Brown, Gabriele Gradoni, Mohsen Khalily, Rahim Tafazolli
arxiv-2512-04298.description: Abstract Abstract We experimentally demonstrate enhanced sensitivity of an atom-based Rydberg radio frequency (RF) receiver integrated with a gradient refractive index (GRIN) Luneburg-type metamaterial lens. By analyzing the electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) effect in Cesium vapor, we compare receiver performance with and without the GRIN lens under a 2.2 GHz and a 3.6 GHz far-field excitation.

pmc-10517688.title: Comparison of Baseline and Test Day Cardiovascular Parameters, Anxiety Scores and Coffee Consumption Among Medical Students Undergoing Objective Structured Clinical Examinations in Jordan
pmc-10517688.creator: Hussein Alhawari, Sameeha Alshelleh, Osama Alzoubi, Asim N Khanfar, Reem Akiely, Bayan Abdallah, Nada Hajjaj, Saja Alkhalaileh, Yousef Khader
pmc-10517688.description: IntroductionObjective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) are considered an integral part of the assessment process of many schools of medicine worldwide. Close monitoring by examiners, scrutinized interactions with patients, and fear of the unknown, among other factors have been reported to cause psychological stress among students during the examinations period.

pmc-11310646.title: Assessing the Impact of the Mindfulness-Based Body Scan Technique on Sleep Quality in Multiple Sclerosis Using Objective and Subjective Assessment Tools: Single-Case Study
pmc-11310646.creator: Ioannis Iliakis, Maria Anagnostouli, George Chrousos, Amaryllis Mavragani, Ornella Corazza, Ali AL-Asadi, Ali Panahi
pmc-11310646.description: BackgroundMultiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting the central nervous system, often leading to poor sleep quality and diminished quality of life (QoL) for affected patients. Sleep disturbances in MS do not always correlate linearly with other symptoms such as anxiety, depression, fatigue, or pain.

pmc-11342476.title: Experience and satisfaction of participants in colorectal cancer screening programs: a qualitative evidence synthesis
pmc-11342476.creator: Cristina Hortalà, Clara Selva, Ivan Sola, Anna Selva
pmc-11342476.description: BackgroundExperience and satisfaction of colorectal cancer screening program participants are among the key factors that determine adherence to these programs. Understanding them is crucial to ensure future participation.ObjectivesTo explore and gain understanding on the experience and satisfaction of the average-risk population participating in colorectal cancer screening programs.MethodsA Qualitative Evidence Synthesis.

pmc-11352914.title: Comparison of Weekly Paclitaxel Regimens in Recurrent Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer: A Single Institution Retrospective Study
pmc-11352914.creator: Laurence Morin, Louis-Philippe Grenier, Nicolas Foucault, Éric Lévesque, François Fabi, Eve-Lyne Langlais, Alexandra Sebastianelli, Marianne Lavoie, Marc Lalancette, Marie Plante, Mahukpe Narcisse Ulrich Singbo, Vincent Castonguay
pmc-11352914.description: Weekly paclitaxel (WP) is a chemotherapeutic cornerstone in the management of patients with platinum-resistant ovarian carcinoma. Multiple WP dosing regimens have been used clinically and studied individually. However, no formal comparison of these regimens is available to provide objective guidance in clinical decision making.

pmc-11712789.title: Significance of Donanemab Versus Placebo in Alzheimer’s Disease Pathogenesis. A Systematic Review
pmc-11712789.creator: Arid Barragán Ortíz, Marcos Arreola Flores, Christan J Monge Ortega, Sofia Andrade Lara, David A Chávez Castillo, Sergio M Carrillo Rodríguez, Thania F Estrada Ortega, Maria F Estrada Posadas, Gilberto Mauricio Suárez
pmc-11712789.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s Disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disease, characterized by a decrease in cognitive and behavioral functions of patients. Between the multiple potential disease‐modifying therapeutics for AD, we have monoclonal antibodies as aducanumab, lecanemab, and donanemab. Recent results from the TRAILBLAZER‐ALZ trial, highlighted donanemab as a promising monoantibodies treatment of early symptomatic AD.

pmc-12456219.title: Short-term transcriptional memory and association-forming ability of tomato plants in response to ultrasound and drought stress stimuli
pmc-12456219.creator: Dóra Farkas, Anita Király, Viktor Ambrus, Bianka Tóth, Judit Dobránszki
pmc-12456219.description: Plant memory is an adaptive mechanism that plants can use to increase their fitness and cope with adverse environmental stresses. In this study, mRNA-sequencing (mRNA-seq), whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) and real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) methods were applied for evaluating formation and maintenance of somatic transcriptional memory after treatment with ultrasound and drought stimuli in tomatoes.

pmc-12462384.title: PerseuCPP: a machine learning strategy to predict cell-penetrating peptides and their uptake efficiency
pmc-12462384.creator: Rayane Monique Bernardes-Loch, Gustavo de Oliveira Almeida, Igor Teixeira Brasiliano, Wagner Meira Jr, Douglas E V Pires, Maria Cristina Baracat-Pereira, Sabrina de Azevedo Silveira, Yoshihiro Yamanishi
pmc-12462384.description: MotivationCell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) are promising tools for transporting therapeutic molecules into cells without damaging the cellular membrane. These peptides serve as efficient drug delivery systems, capable of carrying diverse biologically active substances while exhibiting low cytotoxicity compared to non-native molecules.

pmc-12819405.title: Flow boiling-driven intensive growth of critical minerals during short-lived events
pmc-12819405.creator: Shen Gao, Atsushi Okamoto, Satoshi Matsuno, Edward L. Vinis, Otgonbayar Dandar, Xinyu Zou, Ross N. Mitchell, Jiajun Liu, Kezhang Qin, Hong Xu
pmc-12819405.description: Enrichment of critical metal tellurium (Te) in shallow crustal settings is often linked to hydrothermal boiling, yet the mechanisms driving Te-silica co-precipitation under dynamic fluid flow conditions remain unresolved. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that boiling during fluid flow triggers intensive enrichment of Te and silica at rates >14× faster than non-boiling systems.

pmc-13112334.title: Antinociceptive Effect of Cinnamaldehyde in Male Mice: Investigation of the Mechanisms of Action Through In Silico and In Vivo Approaches
pmc-13112334.creator: Renaly I. de A. Rêgo, Hugo F. O. Pires, Arthur L. Dias, Maria Caroline R. B. Remigio, Humberto H. N. de Andrade, Pablo R. da Silva, Natália F. de Sousa, Luciana Scotti, Marcus T. Scotti, Mirian G. S. S. Salvadori, Ricardo D. de Castro
pmc-13112334.description: Cinnamaldehyde (CA), a major component of Cinnamomum spp. essential oils, has recognized bioactivity, including possible analgesic effects. However, its acute antinociceptive mechanisms remain unclear. This study assessed the influence of CA (15, 30, and 60 mg/kg, p.o.) on locomotor and exploratory behaviors via rotarod and open field tests in male Swiss mice.

pmc-13343947.title: A phase-variable capsule facilitates Akkermansia muciniphila colonization of the intestinal mucus layer
pmc-13343947.creator: Liam Gracia, Elizabeth R. Hughes, Dustin R. Middleton, Katherine D. Mueller, Jessica A. Portillo, Agastya Sharma, Lauren Davey, Maria E. Panzetta, Rachael B. Chanin, Ami S. Bhatt, Raphael H. Valdivia

pmc-13495475.title: Catheter-assisted evacuation through limited laminectomy for traumatic long-segment spinal epidural hematoma in ankylosing spondylitis: a technical note and two case reports
pmc-13495475.creator: Jie Shang, Bao Jia, MUSTAFA ABBAS FARHOOD SULTANI, Lei Liu, Jianwei Zhang, Jie Chen, Xianyi Zhang, Liang Guo, Peipei Li, Meng Han
pmc-13495475.description: BackgroundPatients with ankylosing spondylitis (AS) are prone to unstable spinal fractures with long-segment spinal epidural hematoma (LSEH). Conventional multilevel laminectomy can achieve complete decompression but may disrupt the posterior tension complex. In this article, we describe a catheter-assisted technique for evacuating LSEH through a limited laminectomy window.

pmc-13627906.title: A quantitative screening strategy based on activity-content ratio for prioritizing bioactive compounds in medicinal plants
pmc-13627906.creator: Lin Chen, Xinxin Chen, Shengnan Pi, Ditong Huang, Manhuayun Zhai, Jincai Wang, Zhengjin Jiang, Tingting Zhang
pmc-13627906.description: Accurately evaluating the intrinsic bioactivity of individual constituents, independent of their abundance, remains a major challenge in natural product screening. To address this, we proposed the activity-content ratio (ACR) as a novel index for direct intrinsic inhibitory potency characterization of constituents. Utilizing an at-line nanofractionation platform, an ACR-based screening method for acetylcholinesterase inhibitors was established.

pmc-13637150.title: Polygonatum sibiricum polysaccharides regulate chondrocyte inflammation and metabolism via S100A9 inhibition-mediated autophagy promotion to ameliorate osteoarthritis
pmc-13637150.creator: Shida Kuang, Qiyou Ding, Li Lin, Linhu Li, Zhewen Liu, Qinghu He, Qingfeng Du
pmc-13637150.description: Background Polygonatum sibiricum (P. sibiricum) polysaccharides (PSP), the main bioactive component in the roots of the medicinal and edible plant P. sibiricum, have been shown to exhibit strong anti-inflammatory activity. However, the role of PSP in alleviating osteoarthritis (OA)-related cartilage degeneration and the underlying mechanism—particularly its association with autophagy—remain elusive.
